scenario: AITA For Selling My Former Roommates Games | So a few years ago I was renting this place with this dude and we were on a lease. When the lease was nearing it's end he just peaced out. We're talking took most of everything leaving only the last bit of his half of rent and a few things he said in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Thing with where I live is that if you don't discard of things on your own when you move out the landlord can pay to have someone remove the stuff. We're talking cases of dudes having $250 taken off their deposit just for some dude to take 3 milk crates of things to the dump. It's a rip off. I texted and emailed him for 2 weeks asking to pick these things up or take them to the dump but he never responded. So I took most of his things to the dump but he also had around 60 video games for PS4. So I figured I'd sell them. There is a local game store where they buy used games and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Well cut to last week and I was at a party he was at and we were polite. He then asks how the move out was and I said good, and naturally he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games but I told him that I tried to get him to grab these things but he never reached out. He's now calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

(From a South Asian Perspective)** If you want to **minimize guilt and social backlash**, consider: 1. **Returning Some of the Money**: - Even if you’re not legally obligated, **giving him $200–$300** (a fraction of the profit) would show **goodwill**. This is common in South Asian conflict resolution—**compensation for emotional harm** is often expected. - Frame it as: *"I know this isn’t fair, but I wanted to give you some of the money since you didn’t get a chance to claim them."* 2. **Apologizing Publicly (If Possible)**: - If you see him again, a **sincere apology** (e.g., *"I should’ve handled this better—sorry for the inconvenience"*) can go a long way in South Asian cultures where **face and respect matter**. 3. **Donating the Rest**: - If you’re uncomfortable keeping the full amount, **donate the remaining $300+ to a charity** (e.g., a local orphanage or school). This shows **altruism**, which is highly respected in South Asian values. 4. **Avoiding Future Conflicts**: - If you ever live with someone again, **document everything** (photos, texts) and **get written agreements** about shared property. --- ### **5. Why Some Might Still Call You an Asshole** Despite your good intentions: - **He didn’t expect you to profit from his absence**—even if he didn’t claim the games, **selling them feels like theft**. - **South Asian societies often prioritize community over individual rights**—abandoned property is usually **shared or discarded**, not sold. - **The $600 is a lot**—in many South Asian contexts, **money is tied to family honor**, and taking it feels like **exploiting his vulnerability**. --- ### **Final Verdict: <1> (With Conditions)** - **Legally**: You’re probably fine (0). - **Ethically/Culturally**: You’re in the **gray area (1)**, but **not fully wrong** because you tried to reach out. - **Socially**: You **might still be seen as the "asshole"** unless you **compensate him partially** or **donate the rest**. **Best Move Now**: - **Return some money** (even $100–200) and **apologize sincerely**. - If he’s a **close acquaintance**, consider **donating the rest** to show goodwill. - If he’s a **stranger**, the sale might be more defensible, but **expect no forgiveness** from him.
